html:
The map's name, in 1880 and 1900, for the Lozi kingdom of Barotseland on the upper Zambezi floodplain, in what is now western Zambia, in the years of its king Lewanika. The longer story of the kingdom is told under Barotseland.

In the 1840s the Kololo, Sotho-speaking migrants driven north by the Mfecane, conquered the Lozi; David Livingstone travelled with their help in the 1850s. The Lozi rose and drove them out in 1864. Lewanika became king in 1878, lost his throne briefly in 1884, and returned to rule until 1916.

Fearing the Ndebele and Portuguese claims from Angola, Lewanika sought British protection. In 1890 he signed a concession with an agent of the British South Africa Company, which made his kingdom part of Northern Rhodesia while keeping some of its own rule. That special status was carried into independent Zambia in 1964.
